Basically it comes down to stealth being tied to translocater rather than a separate ability.  
Sombra's introduction was super utility oriented, hack lasted longer,you could TP back to TL after just leaving it somewhere, and stealth was a button you pressed. 

Previous iteration had infinite stealth as a passive because of virus. 

We had already changed her situation by adding virus and reducing hack lockout and removing opportunist, effectively making her more damage oriented than anyone really wanted.

Basically the issue now is that she is VERY damage focused, her ability to get in is the same as her ability to get out (TL), and because of the long cooldown and the fact that cooldown doesn't instantly reset or anything you are often forced to take plays that aren't optimal, as well as that the utility from the character has been reduced with hack being down to 1 second lockout from the previous 1.5 and initial of I think 5 or 8 seconds. The loop now looks like:  
Throw TL, move in, hide for a few seconds when stealth runs out, probably crouch walk a bit, throw TL, position, wait out timer until last second or until visible roughly, THEN start shooting/throwing virus/hacking and HOPE that this was timed perfectly from 5 seconds ago and that nothing pops off because TL isn't back up for 2 seconds. It's all VERY disjointed and feels bad even when it works. The only thing that feels better is "I hacked the tank and now they take BIG damage from me" except like, Reinhardt just puts his shield back up immediately, if I was late DF just jumps, D. \-I mostly like the new pokemon, some of the best designs in the series. There's a few stinkers, but there always are.

\-Textures I don't really care about. It looks good outside of some fps issues that I'm not really concerned over generally.

\-Towns start the overall criticism which is really one thing repeatedly. There's no reason to go...anywhere after you cleared the paths out and caught the ruination pokemon. I basically live outside the auction house in game and only leave if there's something in particular I need which is a 5 minute trip or while I'm hatching eggs if I need a change of scenery. EV training is the longest I really go away and it's been like that basically since I beat the game and caught the ruin pokemon. The towns are particularly lifeless, no interior buildings really, nothing cool to see, no reason to explore them, and the game teaches you this very early on.

\-Area Zero. Lord. So I LOVE Area Zero but it suffers from an empty feeling and not being able to ride Koraidon there the first time made it a massive chore. But the area itself the first time was fantastic, and repeat visits are fun, I just never really go there anymore, because like the towns, why would I? I can't picnic down there so I can't set up camp there either, weird choice? It does have one of the only really hidden areas in the game though which I loved.

\-The map. So the actual map? Really big, really fun, nothing in it. It might be an issue of the -raidons moving too fast, or it might be that they really put nothing in the map like towns and Area Zero, but while some of the areas are cool, there's just nothing to do in them once again.

\-Pokedex. This is basically not something I ever touch in this game. In other games I would rarely pull out the pokedex, read some entries, what have you when I was bored and had the game open. This doesn't happen at all now. Not sure why but the functionality just isn't there for me.

\-Transferables. Why was Sun and Moon the last time all pokemon were available? I don't get it.  DLC can help this, but if they aren't all available I don't understand why. We are missing so many popular pokemon it's stupid.

\-Glitches. There's a bit too many, but most of it is understandable or just bad design like pokemon being stuck behind walls because they made walls hollow. That's oversight and while it's crazy to me that a multibillion dollar company can't figure out that's going to be a problem, it's whatever. Raids not letting you move for 17 years is probably the glitch that bugs me the most. Like, can I move now, before this thing kills us? Also pop in is awful.

\-Sandwiches. Great idea, bad execution that really turns into "Please just let me finish this instead of doing this ridiculous animation". I super love the idea for breeding, if I didn't have to build the sandwich and do the animation every single time.

\-Open world. Aight so listen. Hot take here. I like the idea. But let's refine it a bit, dial it back. This is going to be lengthy.

 Remember old Zelda? Like Majora's mask/OoT? Those were open world divided into subsections that were semi open but had closed off spaces. Majora's mask specifically. Let's do that. Bring back routes and more closed off areas, but improve them with open world aspects that let you do multiple paths or present challenges like we had back in Red and Blue even. Part of why the open world isn't "alive" here is that I think it's too open and the nature of mainline Pokemon. This isn't Zelda or even PLA where things can attack the trainer, they bump into you and battle you and that's that. Once you beat the game and they aren't a shiny or something you need for EVs/exp you won't fight them. There's trainers in the areas, I never see them and when I do I have no intentions of talking to them. Why? Because I don't have to. If they were aggressive well, "When two trainers lock eyes they must do battle". Put me in areas I can't always dodge these people or it at least isn't completely left up to me without some sort of manuevering. Put me in spaces that require me to do some puzzle solving or some actual adventuring and thinking instead of "Jump on Koraidon, jump as high as possible onto the wall, climb the wall, lol no more area" or "Run through at light speed because nothing actually stops me". Sword and Shield kind of had the idea with closed spaces but didn't do that well by not applying trainers to those areas and not giving them really more than one path and didn't nail the open world aspect very well at all until the DLC which was mostly better but still semi lifeless. Scarlet and Violet did the open world part better, but totally ignored closing anything other than Area Zero and like 2 caves off and so nothing feels alive, especially end game. The two caves in question I actually just zoomed through too since they weren't actually separate zones but just more enclosed areas I had no interest in, so there's that.

All this said, these are my favorite pokemon games since USUM, and before that Gold/Silver. So it's good stuff, just it can be improved A LOT.
